_comment: Direction axes the dealer samples from. Derived from Larpo's divergence contract (larpo-knowledge-base/inbox/2026-09-01-hero-divergence-and-design-research.md), knowledge/web/teardown-synthesis.md and knowledge/web/creative-direction.md. Add options freely; never delete one just because it was dealt badly once.

hero_class.note: Visitor understands input, action, transformation or decision from believable interface evidence.
Frame establishes desire, worldview or category position; must not masquerade as product proof.
Argument-led: a claim set like an article or manifesto, with one artifact as evidence.
The hero is a small working tool or demo the visitor can use immediately.

structure.note: One edge-to-edge scene; type lives inside it.
Narrow fixed rail carries identity/nav/CTA; the wide field is the artifact.
Mirror of left rail; copy sits at the field and the rail holds meta.
Numbered list/table as the hero, switchable views.
Type is the composition; one centred statement with disciplined negative space.
A wide horizontal strip of content crosses the fold; stacked bands below.
The product UI is the page, cropped large, headline set inside or over it.
Two asymmetric columns like a magazine spread, caption and pull-quote logic.
Large subject cropped off-frame; copy sits in the remaining space.
One typographic or illustrative poster with minimal chrome.
Hero is chapter one of several full-height chapters, each with its own composition.
Pannable or layered canvas; elements positioned in 2D space.
A literal before/after or state boundary divides the frame.
Dense, live-feeling field of evidence (numbers, events, logs) with a clear focal point.

type_voice.note: Plain, precise sans; hierarchy by size and weight only.
Warm open sans with calligraphic cues.
Tight neo-grotesque used at unusually large or unusually small scale.
High-contrast or old-style serif display with a quiet sans for UI.
Slab or industrial display with a plain text face.
Condensed display, uppercase or sentence case, poster-scale.
Monospace as real data language beside a sans for prose.
Variable font with width/weight/optical axes doing expressive work.
Geometric display face with character; humanist text face.
Serif for body copy as well, sans reserved for controls.

palette_temperature.note: Slate, glacier, steel; cool neutrals, restrained accent.
Moss, sage, clay; low chroma, organic.
Bleached warm neutrals, terracotta or ochre accent.
One loud signal colour on disciplined neutrals.
Deep desaturated darks with a single luminous point.
One hue family, tonal depth carries hierarchy.
Paper ground, ink text, one spot colour; print logic.
A full saturated colour field as the ground.
Palette and pattern drawn from a specific cultural or material reference.

cta_grammar.note: Solid button, clear label; fine when everything else is distinctive.
Typographic link-style action with strong underline/arrow behaviour.
Input or command-palette style entry point.
Very large block action that is a section of its own.
Choose-your-path pair that resolves a real question.
Action pinned to a viewport edge.
Control whose shape or behaviour comes from the product (dial, toggle, stamp, key).

nav_grammar.note: Logo, links, action; keep it if proportions and type are authored.
Wordmark and a single menu trigger.
Nav is a visible numbered index.
Links sit inside the hero composition instead of a bar.
Keyboard-first command palette with a visible hint.
Docked to an edge with square or product-native geometry; never a floating pill.

motion_signature.note: No motion; craft in type, crop and detail.
Pointer-driven response with a still fallback.
Slow loop that expresses product behaviour.
A real decision or state change plays out in the hero.

proof_artifact.note: Input to action to outcome shown as real interface.
Real before/after with the boundary as the hero.
Believable live data with a focal readout.
The product's output as a document, report or message.
Code, diff, CLI or API response.
System, route or architecture drawn precisely.
Specific numbers set large with their source.
